script: A 400-year-old shiplock from a Welsh wreck reveals a four-letter code.
CT scans showed notches matching letters in a hidden combination.
The code is ANCE — a discovery that matches historical context.
Experts say the lock once protected a chest with valuable items.
The lock's condition and date make it a rare, well-preserved find.
Was ANCE a personal code, or something more mysterious?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
A 400-year-old brass lock from the Ann Francis shipwreck off Wales' coast was unlocked using CT scans, revealing a four-letter code: ANCE. The lock, found in 1996 at Margam Beach, is in exceptional condition and may have secured a chest with valuable items like documents or textiles. Researchers note this is a rare example of a well-preserved Elizabethan combination lock linked to a dated wreck. Experts say the code may have had personal significance to its owner. Source: Phys.org, https://phys.org/news/2026-11-ct-scans-reveal-letter-code.html
Full case file: https://youtu.be/X8newfre5Ds
